correctness.rationale: The source concurrence numerator reconstructs exactly as \(A-B-4C\), so its positive-temperature zero is \(e^{6J_1/T}=e^{(2J_1+4J)/T}+4\). With \(u=J_1/T\) and \(r=J/J_1\) this gives the claimed one-variable equation. For every \(r<1\), the derivative in \(u\) is positive on \(u>0\), so the positive root is unique; implicit differentiation gives \(u'(r)>0\). At \(r=1-\delta\), the exact equation forces \(\delta u\to0\) and \(\delta u e^{6u}\sim1\), yielding the Lambert-W law. At \(r=0\), the substitution \(z=e^{2u}\) gives \(z^3-z-4=0\), and differentiating the implicit equation gives the displayed first finite-\(J\) correction. The inspected numerical verifier independently reconstructs the full eight-dimensional Hamiltonian and Wootters concurrence and agrees with these formulas on both signs of \(J\).
